payload.author: exam:3@run-18
payload.body:
examiner (exam-3): writing `tests/lint-ui.test.ts` as five `test` blocks, one per Proof leg, each named for its leg and its Machine clause.

Shape: one memoised probe writes the three temporary files under a single module-level random suffix — the component at `client/src/components/ui/lint-ui-tmp-<rand>.tsx`, the sample at `client/src/lint-ui-tmp-<rand>/Bad.tsx` and the copy at `client/src/components/ui/lint-ui-tmp-<rand>-bad.tsx`, each from the verbatim Proof fence — runs both commands (`node node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js --print-config <sample>` for leg b, `bun run lint:ui -f json` for legs c/d/e) and removes them in a `finally`. Legs (c), (d) and (e) read the *same* run, because (d) only means anything if the ignored copy was on the tree while (c)'s entry was produced. `client/src/components/` does not exist at BASE (Task 1 creates it), so the probe records whether it was there and removes only what it created.

Two readings I am writing down:
  - Leg (c)'s "exactly one entry" is one entry *whose filePath ends with the sample path*, not one entry in the whole array: `-f json` prints one entry per linted file and the app's own seven `no-unknown-classes` findings are on the tree at this wave.
  - The JSON parse of the `bun run` stdout is guarded so that the red line at BASE names the missing script rather than a parse error — at BASE `bun run lint:ui` exits 1 with an empty stdout, which is the same exit code the leg pins, so an unguarded `JSON.parse` would have failed for a reason that reads like a typo.

payload.author: impl:2@run-18
payload.body:
Approach for task 2 (locators by role+name, aria-checked views, tailwind in bundleOf):

1. `types.ts`: add `Locator = string | {role: string; name: string}` and widen `Action`'s three arms to carry it. `actionsOf`/`isCallbackAction` are unchanged — they never read inside an action.
2. `browser.ts`: `nodeFor` becomes a resolver returning a params fragment — `{nodeId}` for a string (today's `DOM.querySelector` path) or `{backendNodeId}` for a `{role,name}` (`Accessibility.queryAXTree` on the document root, first node in tree order, `backendDOMNodeId`). `Accessibility.enable` is sent lazily, once per session, on the first object locator. `centreOf` and `DOM.focus` spread the fragment, so both paths meet at the same Input.* calls. New message: `act: no element matches role=<role> name="<name>"`; the string message stays byte-identical.
3. `render-move.ts`: `checked`/`unchecked` read `aria-checked` as well as `data-checked` (OR), so every BASE view over a reflected DOM still holds.
4. `rules/views.ts`: `readingChecked` reads the same pair, so the fix line names `#a` over a static React render that only carries `aria-checked`.
5. `bundleOf`: `plugins: [tailwind]` from `bun-plugin-tailwind`; `bun-plugin-tailwind@^0.1.2` and `tailwindcss@^4.3.3` into `packages/tinyapp-exam/package.json` dependencies, `bun install` at the root to regenerate `bun.lock`.
6. `index.ts` names `Locator` in its type export from `./types`.

`REFLECT_CHECKED` keeps to `input` elements untouched — writing `data-checked="false"` onto base-ui's span would paint shadcn's checkbox checked.
